task.title: Fix four mistakes
task.description: You are in the folder ~/portfolio. The repository has four mistakes - fix each one with the right command: 1) Look at git status and git log --oneline. 2) The file index.html is broken and not added to the index yet - bring it back to the version from the last commit. 3) The file passwords.txt was added to the index by accident - remove it from the index, but don't delete the file itself. 4) The message of the last commit has a typo (contatcs) - fix the message to Add contacts page without creating a new commit. 5) The commit Change colors to neon is already published on GitHub - undo it with git revert without deleting it from the history (don't use reset --hard). 6) Check the result: git log --oneline and git status.
task.starter_code:
# Write the commands one per line. Lines starting with # are comments.
# You are in the folder ~/portfolio. First look at git status and git log --oneline.

# 1. Bring the broken index.html back to the version from the last commit

# 2. Remove passwords.txt from the index (don't delete the file itself)

# 3. Fix the typo in the message of the last commit: Add contacts page

# 4. Undo the published commit Change colors to neon with git revert

# 5. Check the result: git log --oneline and git status
task.setup:
sim.user.config["user.name"] = "Anna Karimova"; sim.user.config["user.email"] = "anna@example.com"; sim.user.config["init.defaultBranch"] = "main"; sim.run(`mkdir portfolio && cd portfolio && git init echo "

Anna Karimova

" > index.html git add . && git commit -m "Add home page" echo "body { color: navy; }" > style.css git add . && git commit -m "Add styles" echo "body { color: lime; background: magenta; }" > style.css git commit -am "Change colors to neon" echo "

About me

" > about.html git add . && git commit -m "Add about page" echo "

Contacts

" > contacts.html git add . && git commit -m "Add contatcs page" echo "

Anna Karimova

" > index.html echo "admin: qwerty123" > passwords.txt git add passwords.txt`, { quiet: true });

tests.name: index.html is back to the version from the commit
tests.fail: git restore index.html brings the file back to the version from the last commit.

tests.name: git restore is used for index.html
tests.fail: A broken file that is not in the index is brought back with git restore index.html.

tests.name: passwords.txt stayed in the folder and is not in the index
tests.fail: git restore --staged passwords.txt removes the file from the index but doesn't delete it from disk. Don't use rm.

tests.name: passwords.txt did not get into any commit
tests.fail: First remove passwords.txt from the index (step 2), and only then run git commit --amend: amend takes everything in the index into the commit.

tests.name: The typo is fixed with amend, not with a new commit
tests.check: repo.log().find((c) => c.subject === "Add contacts page") !== undefined && "contacts.html" in repo.log().find((c) => c.subject === "Add contacts page").files && repo.commit(repo.log().find((c) => c.subject === "Add contacts page").parents[0]).subject === "Add about page" && repo.log().every((c) => !/cont[a-z]*cts page/.test(c.subject) || c.subject === "Add contacts page")
tests.fail: git commit --amend -m "Add contacts page" replaces the last commit. Run amend before revert, while the commit with the typo is the last one.

tests.name: The bad commit stayed in the history
tests.check: repo.log().find((c) => c.subject === "Change colors to neon") !== undefined
tests.fail: You can't delete a published commit from the history: git revert adds a new undo commit, and the old one stays.

tests.name: The last commit is Revert "Change colors to neon"
tests.check: repo.commit("HEAD").subject === "Revert \"Change colors to neon\"" && repo.commit("HEAD~1").subject === "Add contacts page"
tests.fail: git revert --no-edit HEAD~2 after amend (or git revert <hash of the commit Change colors to neon>).

tests.name: style.css is again as in the commit Add styles
tests.check: sim.read("~/portfolio/style.css") === repo.log().find((c) => c.subject === "Add styles").files["style.css"] && repo.commit("HEAD").files["style.css"] === repo.log().find((c) => c.subject === "Add styles").files["style.css"]
tests.fail: Undo exactly the commit Change colors to neon. Find it in git log --oneline.

tests.name: The rest of the work is not lost: 6 commits, about.html and contacts.html are in place
tests.check: repo.log().length === 6 && "about.html" in repo.commit("HEAD").files && "contacts.html" in repo.commit("HEAD").files && sim.exists("~/portfolio/about.html") && sim.exists("~/portfolio/contacts.html")
tests.fail: There were 5 commits, amend replaces a commit (doesn't add one), revert adds one: you should get 6. Don't use reset --hard.

tests.name: git reset --hard is not used
tests.fail: You don't need reset --hard in this task: it erases work and rewrites history.

tests.name: The working directory is clean except for passwords.txt
tests.fail: At the end, git status should show only Untracked files: passwords.txt.

tests.name: Other data: all four mistakes are fixed
tests.check: repo.status().modified.length === 0 && repo.status().untracked.includes("passwords.txt") && repo.log().every((c) => !("passwords.txt" in c.files)) && repo.log().length === 6 && repo.log().find((c) => c.subject === "Add contacts page") !== undefined && repo.log().find((c) => c.subject === "Change colors to neon") !== undefined && repo.commit("HEAD").subject === "Revert \"Change colors to neon\"" && sim.read("~/portfolio/style.css") === repo.log().find((c) => c.subject === "Add styles").files["style.css"]
tests.fail: The solution must not depend on hashes: use HEAD~2 or find the hash in git log --oneline.
tests.setup:
sim.user.config["user.name"] = "Anna Karimova"; sim.user.config["user.email"] = "anna@example.com"; sim.user.config["init.defaultBranch"] = "main"; sim.run(`mkdir portfolio && cd portfolio && git init echo "

Aziz Rakhimov

" > index.html git add . && git commit -m "Add home page" echo "h1 { font-size: 32px; }" > style.css git add . && git commit -m "Add styles" echo "h1 { font-size: 120px; }" > style.css git commit -am "Change colors to neon" echo "

I am a web developer

" > about.html git add . && git commit -m "Add about page" echo "

aziz@example.com

" > contacts.html git add . && git commit -m "Add contcts page" echo "" > index.html echo "root: 0000" > passwords.txt git add passwords.txt`, { quiet: true });

tests.name: The script runs without internal errors
tests.fail: Check the quotes in your commands.

hints: Start with git status: Git suggests the commands itself in brackets - git restore <file> and git restore --staged <file>.
The order matters: first git restore --staged passwords.txt, then git commit --amend - otherwise the password gets into the commit.
The message of the last commit: git commit --amend -m "Add contacts page". The number of commits doesn't change.
After amend, the bad commit is third from the top, that is HEAD~2. You can also give its hash from git log --oneline.
git revert --no-edit HEAD~2 creates the commit Revert "Change colors to neon" and brings style.css back.

questions.question: git status shows index.html under Changes not staged for commit. You want to throw away these edits and bring back the version from the last commit. Which command?
questions.explanation: git restore file brings the file in the working directory back to the version from the index (which matches the last commit). Unsaved edits are lost.

questions.question: What does git restore --staged passwords.txt do with a new file that you added by accident with git add?
options: Removes the file from the index; the file stays in the folder as Untracked
Deletes the file from all commits
Makes a commit without this file
questions.explanation: --staged works only with the index: the file is no longer prepared for the commit, but it stays on disk.

questions.question: Match each situation with the right command.
pairs: You broke a file and haven't run git add yet
You added an extra file to the index
A typo in the message of the last commit, which is not published yet
You need to undo a commit that is already on GitHub
questions.explanation: Each level of a mistake (working directory → index → local commit → published commit) needs its own command: the "deeper" the mistake, the more careful the fix.

questions.question: Why is git revert safe for published history, and git reset is not?
options: revert adds a new undo commit and doesn't change old commits, while reset moves the branch back and "throws away" commits
questions.explanation: Your teammates already have the published commits. revert only adds a commit on top, so their copies of the history stay correct.

questions.question: What is true about git commit --amend?
options: It replaces the last commit with a new one that has a different hash
It takes everything that is in the index now into the commit
It is safe to use for a commit that is already sent to GitHub
With -m, it changes the message of the last commit
questions.explanation: amend creates a new commit in place of the last one (a new hash) and adds the contents of the index. You must not change published commits this way.

questions.question: Match each git reset HEAD~1 mode with what happens to the changes from the undone commit.
pairs: They stay in the index (ready to commit)
They stay in the working directory, but not in the index
They are erased from both the index and the working directory
questions.explanation: All three modes move the branch to HEAD~1. The difference is how many areas they "roll back" after the branch.

questions.question:
Git printed:
HEAD is now at c8a4ab7 Add styles
Which command was most likely run?
questions.explanation: The line HEAD is now at ... is the output of git reset --hard: the branch and the files were moved to the given commit.

questions.question: After git reset --hard, a commit you need is gone. Which command shows the log of all HEAD movements so that you can find its hash? Type the whole command.
questions.explanation: git reflog is a "time machine": it remembers where HEAD pointed, even after reset.

questions.question:
git reflog shows:
c8a4ab7 (HEAD -> main) HEAD@{0}: reset: moving to HEAD~1
b7886e2 HEAD@{1}: commit: Add about page
How do you bring back the lost commit Add about page?
questions.explanation: reset --hard to the hash from the reflog (or HEAD@{1}) brings the branch and the files back to that commit.

questions.question: Which commands rewrite history (change or remove existing commits)?
questions.explanation: amend replaces the last commit, reset moves the branch back. revert adds a new commit, and restore doesn't touch commits at all.

questions.question: Complete the command that undoes commit 8401f68 with a new commit without opening an editor: git ________ --no-edit 8401f68
questions.explanation: git revert --no-edit 8401f68 creates a commit Revert "..." with the opposite changes.

questions.question: You ran git reset --soft HEAD~1. What will git status show?
options: nothing to commit, working tree clean
The changes of the undone commit under Changes to be committed
questions.explanation: --soft moves only the branch: the changes of the commit stay in the index, and you can commit them again right away.
